title: 1,500 Years on a Cliff, Held by 27 Beams — Shanxi's Hanging Temple | China Travel Expert
description:
For 1,500 years, a temple has hung off a sheer cliff in Shanxi — held up by just 27 wooden beams, 75 meters above the ground.

The Hanging Temple (Xuankong Si) in Hunyuan County, Datong, was first built in the late Northern Wei dynasty (around 491 AD). Its slender-looking stilts are largely decorative — the real load is carried by crossbeams driven deep into the rock face, reinforced with iron. It's the only temple in China dedicated to three faiths at once: Buddhism, Taoism and Confucianism. It was built high on the cliff partly to escape flooding from the valley below.

🧭 Expert Tip: Arrive right at opening. The plank walkways are narrow and limit how many people can be on the structure at once, so early means almost no crowds — and the best photos.
